This game really is a mix between Destiny 2 and Warframe, and in some ways that is great, but it also copies all of the grindy micro-transaction Cr*p too and amplifies it.

This game paid money bullsh*t is terrible. Im not joking when I say this. I honestly think it will take some people months or even a year to get most of the classes. I have seen some people grind over 20 hours for 1 component for an ultimate class, of which require 5 components and 4 of them require additional materials. And once that's all done, you still have to wait 36 hours for it to complete. 

Warframe was much more fair in this matter. Yes, this game copies a lot of its paid money shop style, but at least Warframe lets you obtain the paid currency much easier, either by trading items you have multiples of or giving discounts up to 75% off the premium currency. 

One of the biggest shocking moments for me was when I looked at how much it would cost to max out your inventory... around 500 dollars/euros... This is a fricken Looter Shooter game that limits your inventory size unless you grind your ass off to MR 30, which only doubles it (its a progressive increase) to a max of 150 (for weapons and slotted components, which by the way drop all the time). 


The paid shop in this game honestly gets me angry. and I'm usually a very chill dude.

As an official content creator for the game, I figured now would be the best time to give a review.

First and front, this game is.... lack of a better term, a looter shooter, grind fest. End game is all about grinding to unlock all characters that are locked, and further than that their ultimate's. It can be very time consuming and furthermore tedious but it does pay off, especially not having to spend money to insta-unlock, 

I have spent money, only on the battle pass, obviously since its the only thing currently worth it to spend my tight budget on, no complaints there, battlepasses are common place in games today.

The only complaints I have so far would be about optimization and the drop chances.

Optimization is slowly getting better, however my PC struggles playing the game still yet (its near top of the line and shouldn't). I still don't know why but hopefully one day it won't.

Drop chances, still need to be hella improved, I get it, its a free to play game and the devs gotta make money. But spending hours on hours not getting the AMPs or even that matter the parts for descendants is a little disheartening since you would think there would be a pity system in place.

Overall I would rate this game 8/10, its a pretty solid looter shooter and has it place in the same hall that houses Warframe and Destiny 2 with its slightly own blend of the style of game. It still needs improvements and if those happen, I will gladly come update the review. ^_^

Engaging experience

The First Descendant is an exciting addition to the sci-fi RPG genre, blending a captivating storyline with dynamic gameplay. You play as a Descendant, uncovering ancient secrets and battling foes in a stunningly crafted universe.

Pros:

Immersive Story: A well-crafted narrative that keeps you engaged.
Engaging Combat: Fluid, strategic combat with a robust skill tree.
Stunning Visuals: Beautiful, detailed environments enhance immersion.
Co-op Multiplayer: Team up with friends for challenging missions.
Customization: Extensive options for tailoring your character.
Cons:

Microtransactions: Can feel intrusive and detract from the experience.
Grind-heavy Progression: Advancing can require repetitive gameplay.
Server Issues: Occasional stability problems, especially in multiplayer.
Balancing: Some character classes and abilities need tweaking.

Despite its drawbacks, The First Descendant is a fantastic sci-fi RPG that offers a lot of excitement and depth, making it a worthy addition to any RPG fan’s library.

The game play and upgrade system is very similar to Warframe with a mission/ activity loop that will be familiar to Destiny players.

Yes the prices in the cash shop are expensive... but most things are easier to grind for than the haters will have you believe. Honestly the biggest grind is the weapons which can't be purchased anyway so the shop is mostly just there to provide "Premium" character skins to those desperate enough to pay for them.

So far it's pretty fun. As I play more i'll as usual update the review.

In essence the game is a mixture of Destiny and Warframe.
Favouring third person shooting mechanics with some hero powers, you operate in a setting that flavor wise is a bit à la Destiny Space Fantasy with a dabbling of Warframe oddness.

It's definitely an Action FPS Looter/Shooter with a lot of crafting, looting, customising weapons and leveling.
These mechanics are more in tune with the Warframe approach. 
The card slot mechanic used on your character and your weapons has the Warframe vibe even having the cost efficient slots where card cost is halved.

The setting so far is interesting but has the same flaw Destiny and Warframe has whereas they do love to just throw terms and words at you while hoping not to loose you.
Like Destiny though it does somewhat ease you into it.

I can see one loving to just main a character when you're a dirty casual like me (Ajax for the win!!) or hoard and level up every unlocked character. (you collect resources to do so)
It is accessible, grindy but not insufferable so at first glance. Undoubtedly like Destiny and especially Warframe it will become far far more grindy in endgame. Which some people will love and other hate.
There is a battlepass and a cosmetics store from what i've seen.
Currently I have no intention to dabble into the Battlepass unless the game really catches me.

At the moment from the gameplay i had and what i've experienced I can definitely recommend giving it a go. Perhaps not as your 'lifestyle' game but to dabble in it whenever you feel like it.
It's definitely a good alternative to Destiny and Warfame. It's a quality product though granted not at the level of development or tuning the other 2 are.
...given that this one is new that's not surprising.
So... for now I recommend this one.
